intro: A medium caramel macchiato at a café is about 250 kcal (estimate). Most of it comes from full cream milk and vanilla syrup, not the espresso.
diet: Yes, if you count it as a snack and not just a drink. 250 kcal is about the same as a small plate of rice. The problem is drinking it daily without noticing, because liquid calories add up easily. Make it a treat 1-2 times a week, or ask for a less sweet version.
tips: Ask for half the syrup (1-2 pumps) to save about 30-40 kcal.
Switch to low-fat or skim milk. It still tastes okay.
Pick a small size and have it with something with protein, not with cake.

swap.name: Cappuccino, no sugar (medium)
swap.why: Still milky with a creamy coffee taste, but no syrup. Half the calories, almost the same protein.

faq.q: What's the difference between a caramel macchiato and a latte?
faq.a: A latte is espresso mixed with milk. A caramel macchiato is milk with vanilla syrup, espresso poured on top, then a caramel drizzle. That's why it's sweeter.

faq.q: Does a caramel macchiato have a lot of caffeine?
faq.a: A medium usually has 1-2 espresso shots, about the same as a normal cup of coffee. If you're sensitive, avoid it late in the afternoon.

faq.q: Can I ask for less sweet?
faq.a: Yes. Most cafés can reduce the syrup pumps or skip the caramel drizzle. Just tell them when you order.
